title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the first sheet ('Coh d'E-M I'; the next page is headed 'Coh d'EM VI' and refers back to 'le diagramme (*) en bas de la page I') of a set of notes on the stable (co)homology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces. The style suggests notes taken at, or prepared for, a seminar. In modern language the page computes the four groups π_*(HA∧HB) for A, B ∈ {Z, F_p} in the stable range (degrees < 2n), using Milnor's dual Steenrod algebra.

(0) Recalled facts.
- Cartan–Serre: H^*(K(F_p,n);F_p) is the free graded-commutative algebra on admissible monomials applied to ι_n. For p = 2 these are the monomials of excess < n (a polynomial algebra). For p odd they are the monomials of excess < n, together with those of excess = n whose first (outermost) operation is β.
- A = F_p[P^i, β], with P^0 = 1, Adem relations, deg P^i = 2i(p−1), deg β = 1. For p = 2, A is generated by Sq^i with Adem relations Sq^aSq^b = Σ_j (…) Sq^{a+b−j}Sq^j for a < 2b.
- The dual is A_* = Sym(ξ_i, i>0) ⊗ Λ(τ_j, j≥0), with |ξ_i| = 2p^i−2 and |τ_j| = 2p^j−1. For p = 2 it is Sym(ξ_i) with |ξ_i| = 2^i−1.

(1) Four problems are listed: H_*(K(F_p,n);F_p), H_*(K(Z,n);F_p), H_*(K(F_p,n);Z), H_*(K(Z,n);Z).
- Cartan's answer for a general abelian group G is that, in the stable range, H_*(K(G,n);Z) is a sum of copies of G/pG and _pG.
- Examples: H_{n+2} = G/2G, H_{n+3} = _2G, H_{n+4} = G/2G ⊕ G/3G, H_{n+5} = _2G ⊕ _3G.
- Additivity K(M×N,n) ≃ K(M,n)×K(N,n) is noted.
- For R an F_p-algebra and G of exponent p, H^*(K(G,n);R) is the free anticommutative algebra on Hom(G,R) ⊗ (excess < n part of A).

(2) Bocksteins.
- First Bockstein. Stably, H_*(K(F_p,n);Z) is killed by p: it is π_*(HZ∧HF_p), an F_p-module. So the coefficient sequence Z →p Z → Z/p splits into short exact sequences 0 → H_*(K(F_p,n);Z)/p → H_*(K(F_p,n);F_p) → H_{*−1}(K(F_p,n);Z) → 0. The composite β_1 is a Bockstein on A_*, and it suffices to make β_1 explicit.
- Second Bockstein. The fibration K(Z,n) →p K(Z,n) → K(F_p,n) gives, in degrees < 2n, a second short exact sequence 0 → H_*(K(Z,n);F_p) → H_*(K(F_p,n);F_p) → H_{*−1}(K(Z,n);F_p) → 0 and a second derivation β_2.
- Modern reading: β_1 and β_2 are the Bocksteins acting on the left and right factors of HF_p∧HF_p. Both are derivations of A_*. One of them is τ_0 ↦ 1, τ_i ↦ 0 (i ≠ 0), ξ_j ↦ 0. The other is τ_j ↦ ξ_j, ξ_j ↦ 0 in conjugate generators.

(3) Conclusions.
- H_*(K(F_p,n);Z) is the free divided-power algebra on the excess < n part of the appropriate subquotient of Sym(ξ)⊗Λ(τ).
- β_2 acts on H_*(K(F_p,n);Z) as the derivation τ_j ↦ ξ_j, ξ_j ↦ 0, and Im β_2 = Ker β_2 = H̃_*(K(Z,n);Z)_(p).
- This uses the fact that the positive-degree p-torsion of H_*(HZ;Z) has exponent p. The sequence HZ∧HZ →p HZ∧HZ → HZ∧HF_p then gives 0 → H_k(HZ) → H_k(HF_p;Z) → H_{k−1}(HZ) → 0.

(4) Conjugation.
- Milnor/Steenrod conjugation c on A and on A_* exchanges the two β's.
- It carries the stable part of H_*(K(Z,n);F_p) isomorphically onto H_*(K(F_p,n);Z) inside A_*. This is diagram (*).
- This is the stable form of Cartan's symmetry H_*(K(G,n);H) ≅ H_*(K(H,n);G). The next page proves it by Dold–Thom, Eilenberg–Zilber and swapping the factors of the smash product.

Role in the dossier: the notes sit in a file on the divided-power de Rham complex, next to notes on Milnor K_2, Gersten–Quillen resolutions and Ext^2(Z, G_m). This is plausibly background for Breen-style computations of Ext(G_a, G_a) and of MacLane homology via Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, where divided powers appear naturally. The page itself is an expository summary of classical algebraic topology.
errors: The 'Conclusion' writes H_*(K(F_p,n);Z) as the divided-power algebra on the excess<n part of all of Sym(ξ_i)⊗Λ(τ_j), j≥0. The integral homology should be only the kernel (= image) of the relevant Bockstein, e.g. Sym(ξ_i)⊗Λ(τ_j, j≥1) up to conjugation, not the whole A_*. As written it is sloppy.

'L'homologie est entièrement de torsion première' (exponent p) holds only in the stable range. Unstably, H_*(K(Z/2,2);Z) has Z/4 torsion (Pontryagin square), so the claim needs the 'deg < 2n' restriction stated later.

In the stable range the multiplicative ('divided power algebra') structure is vacuous, since products land in degrees ≥ 2n. The divided-power statement is really Cartan's unstable theorem, here conflated with the stable computation.
The Adem relation is written with the binomial coefficients and the upper summation limit [a/2] left blank. This is incomplete but not wrong.
The excess=n clause for p odd ('qui se termine par β') is ambiguous as to order. The correct condition is that the outermost operation (ε_1 = 1) is β.

ideas.what: Cartan–Serre computation of H^*(K(F_p,n);F_p) as a free graded-commutative algebra on admissible monomials of bounded excess
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Cartan theorem on cohomology of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces

ideas.what: Dual Steenrod algebra A_* = P(ξ_i)⊗Λ(τ_j) with degrees 2p^i−2, 2p^j−1, and the conjugation c
The two Bocksteins as derivations of A_* (left/right action on HF_p∧HF_p), with Im = Ker giving H_*(K(Z,n);Z)_(p)
ideas.modern_name: Bockstein actions on π_*(HF_p∧HF_p); integral homology of HZ and HF_p

ideas.modern_name: Stable integral homology of K(G,n) / H_*(HZ;Z)

deep.surprise_reason: These are faithful, mostly correct summary notes of classical Cartan–Serre–Milnor results on Eilenberg–MacLane homology, probably seminar notes. The only point of mild interest is their placement in a divided-power de Rham dossier, which suggests use as background for Breen/MacLane-type Ext computations. Nothing new or uncredited appears.
transcription_corrections: Header should read 'Coh d'E-M I' (Cohomologie d'Eilenberg–MacLane I), consistent with the next page's 'Coh d'EM VI'.
The symbol transcribed '(K)' at bottom left is '(*)', the diagram referred to on the next page ('diagramme (*) en bas de la page I').
'$\mathcal{G}$ [-$\mathcal R$-] une F_p-algèbre' should read: G a group and R an F_p-algebra; then H^*(K(G,n),R) for G of characteristic p ('groupes' struck out).
In the conclusion the coefficient Z is written over a struck-through symbol, and the struck word is 'l'autre'.
